newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money edges up on weekend cover.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money edges up on weekend cover.

text.p: * Volume rises to 17.297 billion from 14.339 billion pesos.
Manila overnight money edged up to an average of 10.5625 percent on Monday from 10.53125 after banks covered three days of weekend positions, traders said.
Rates moved from 10.75 to 10.53125 percent, with 28 lenders and 26 borrowers.
"It's stll soft," a trader said, but he said 4.0 billion pesos would be drained this week from the sale of 2-year T-notes.
In secondary trading of T-bills, the market had more buyers than sellers, traders said.
"They're expecting T-bill rates to go down slightly," said another trader, referring to the auction later in the day.
"They'd rather get papers now," he said. He said the high liquidity in the system would pull down rates further.
A Reuter poll of six institutions showed bids from 10.60 to 10.725 percent; 11.125 to 11.20 for six months; and 11.55 to 11.65 for one year.
